title: Fellow Disciple Provocation

text.content:
After three morning bell tolls, the Outer Court Training Grounds of Tianqing Sect filled with Servant Disciples. Chen Ji carried a wooden tray through the crowd, the tray bearing a Qi Supplementing Powder jar destined for the Elixir Chamber. His pace was measured, his expression wearing that habitual timid look, like wild grass waiting to be trampled.

Yet as he passed by Zhao Yue, the latter suddenly stumbled, deliberately crashing into him.

"Bang!" The medicine jar flew from his grasp and shattered against the blue stone floor, brown liquid splattering everywhere.

Chen Ji stared at the mess, fingers tightening imperceptibly—that Qi Supplementing Powder had taken him three days to gather ingredients and refine.

dialogue.content: "Oh dear, so sorry, so sorry." Zhao Yue's smile didn't reach his eyes as he gave a mocking bow. "My legs aren't cooperating today, didn't see Brother Chen passing by. Waste is just waste—can't even dodge people while walking?"

text.content:
Laughter erupted immediately around them. Zhao Yue was the nephew of the Outer Court Steward, and with that connection he bullied others at will, specifically targeting soft targets. Today he wanted to establish his dominance before everyone, and Chen Ji, this "waste," was undoubtedly the perfect target.

Chen Ji slowly lifted his gaze, his eyescalm得像一潭死水. "Brother Zhao broke the medicine jar—you should compensate."

dialogue.content: "Compensate?" Zhao Yue acted as if he'd heard the joke of the century, his voice suddenly rising. "Does garbage refined by atrashdeserve my compensation? This inferior medicine wouldn't even be good enough for dogs! Tianqing Sect's face is being dragged through the mud by you parasites!"

text.content: He stepped hard on the scattered medicine dregs, grinding them beneath his foot. His gaze swept across the watching crowd: "Everyone take a look—this is our Outer Court's 'genius' Chen Ji! Three years and still can't break through to Qi Refining first stage—his ancestors must be turning in their graves from shame!"

dialogue.content: "I heard he only got into Tianqing Sect through connections, tsk, tsk, don't know which Elder had eyes that were blind. Waste is waste—wherever it goes, it only pollutes the air!"

text.content:
The watching disciples joined the heckling, and some even started throwing stones at Chen Ji. Chen Ji had seen this scene many times—every time someone wanted to establish dominance, he would be pulled out as a target. Three years—he'd grown accustomed to it.

But accustomed didn't mean numb.

He lowered his eyes, carving every taunt into his heart. His face still wore that submissive expression, as if truly frightened.

dialogue.content: "What? Cat got your tongue?" Zhao Yue pressed closer, a triumphant smirk on his lips. "Atrashshould havetrash's觉悟, kneel and apologize to me, and we'll call it even. Otherwise..."

text.content:
Chen Ji slowly raised his head, meeting Zhao Yue's gaze. Those eyes were terrifyingly calm—no anger, no fear, only a depth that made Zhao Yue inexplicably uneasy.

"Brother Zhao wants to step on me to build his reputation today—fine." Chen Ji's voice was soft, yet each word came through clearly. "But has Brother ever considered that some debts must eventually be repaid?"

Chen Ji slowly bent his knee, his kneecap striking the cold blue stone floor with a crisp, jarring sound. Laughter burst from the watching crowd.

"That's more like it!" Zhao Yue patted Chen Ji's face triumphantly. "Atrashshould havetrash's样子—got it? Get lost, and don't let me see you again!"

He turned and walked away, steps light as a rooster that had won a fight. The watching disciples gradually dispersed, leaving only Chen Ji kneeling on the ground, surrounded by scattered medicine dregs and frozen mockery.

text.content:
Chen Ji slowly stood up, brushing dust from his knees.

"Brother Zhao says I'mtrash—" he suddenly laughed, that smile gentle yet chilling, "But I seem to recall that last month you lost three spirit stones to me and still owe five taels of silver in gambling debts? Iftrashcan win your spirit stones, what does that make Brother?"

Zhao Yue's face changed drastically; whispers rippled through the crowd.

The crowd gradually dispersed. Chen Ji crouched alone on the ground, gathering the medicine dregs. His movements were light and slow, as if doing something utterly ordinary.

Yet in his mind, a blurry image was taking shape.

The Tianji Record pulsed with warmth—he saw it. One hour later, Zhao Yue would pass alone through that mountain path behind the sect. The terrain there was complex, rarely visited.

Chen Ji picked up the last piece of broken jar and stood. Sunlight fell on his face, revealing eyes utterly different from before—cold, deep, like万年寒冰 hidden within.

trash?

A barely perceptible smile curved his lips. Today you wanted to step on me to build your reputation—tomorrow I'll teach you什么叫无路可逃.

The distant bell announced class dismissal. Chen Ji tucked the fragments into his sleeve and walked unhurriedly toward the Elixir Chamber.

dialogue.content:
"Chen Ji!" A shout came from behind—it was the disciple who had heckled most loudly. "The Steward says to clean the Martial Arena thoroughly today, or no dinner for you!"

Chen Ji's footsteps paused. He turned, his face reassembling that timid smile: "Understood, I'll go right away."

text.content:
He picked up the broom, sweeping the ground stroke by stroke. The spectators had long since left; only his solitary figure remained, stretched long in the morning light.

Sweat slid down his temples, yet Chen Ji seemed oblivious to fatigue. His thoughts had already drifted to a quarter hour later—the Back Mountain path, Zhao Yue alone.

The Tianji Record pulsed warmly again; that image grew increasingly clear.

text.content:
By the time the Martial Arena was spotless, the sun had climbed past midmorning. Chen Ji dropped the broom and silently slipped toward the Back Mountain.

Passing through the Bamboo Grove, evading the mountain patrol disciples, he crouched behind a bush. The vantage point perfectly overlooked the winding path—Zhao Yue's inevitable route.

The Tianji Record pulsed again; the foreseen moment drew near.

text.content:
Chen Ji returned the broom to the storage room and unhurriedly walked toward the Elixir Chamber. He needed to report first—though Elixir Chamber Steward Zhang was harsh, he never arbitrarily docked wages without cause.

As for Zhao Yue... he glanced down at the fragments in his sleeve, a hint of amusement flickering in his eyes.

Why rush? The prey will always come to you eventually.

Inside the Elixir Chamber, Steward Zhang examined the supplies Chen Ji delivered and made a note in his register.

"Alright, that will do for today." He waved dismissively without looking up. "Tomorrow, inventory the herbs in the storage—don't make mistakes."

Chen Ji respectfully acknowledged, then withdrew from the Elixir Chamber.

Exiting the Elixir Chamber, the sun had already shifted westward. Chen Ji stood under the corridor, watching the orange-red clouds dyed across the horizon, silently calculating the time in his heart.

That idiot Zhao Yue should be arriving at the Back Mountain path soon.

He smiled faintly and set off, walking unhurriedly toward the Back Mountain. His gait still carried that timorous manner, shoulders slightly hunched, as if today's humiliation had scared him witless.

But his eyes were clearer than ever.

Passing through the medicinal garden, skirting the Bamboo Grove, Chen Ji arrived at the Back Mountain's outer edge. He didn't rush in, instead stopping behind a massive boulder, sensing the surroundings.

The Tianji Record's warmth told him—Zhao Yue was nearby.

Chen Ji took a deep breath,身形一闪, and vanished into the bushes beside the path. He was like a patient hunter, waiting for his prey to fall into the snare.

text.content:
Chen Ji held his breath, watching Zhao Yue approach along the path. The fellow's face was livid, still clearly stewing over the morning's incident.

Completely unaware of the danger around him.

Chen's fingers slipped silently into his sleeve, gripping a sharp fragment of the medicine jar. His gaze was cold as a blade, yet his lips held a faint, barely perceptible smile.

text.content:
"Brother Zhao, we meet again." Chen Ji's voice drifted from the shadows, sinister, like sound from the Nine Netherworlds.

Zhao Yue jerked his head up, saw Chen Ji's face, and stumbled backward in fright. "You... what are you doing here?!"

Zhao Yue clutched his bleeding neck, his expression a mixture of terror and anger. He never imagined thattrashwho let himself be bullied daily would actually dare touch him!

"Chen Ji... you're insane!" He gritted his teeth. "Do you know who I am? My uncle is the Outer Court Steward! You dare hurt me—I'll make you die without a burial place!"

Chen Ji watched Zhao Yue's fierce-in-appearance-but-terrified-inside state and suddenly laughed.

That smile was gentle, harmless, even carrying a hint of timidity—the exact same expression as when he was humiliated this morning. But Zhao Yue, looking into those eyes, felt cold to his bones.

"Brother Zhao is right." Chen Ji put away the fragments, speaking unhurriedly. "What's atrashafraid of?"

He turned and left, his silhouette stretched long in the sunset. Zhao Yue tried to chase, but discovered his legs had turned to jelly.

Chen Ji gazed at Zhao Yue's departing silhouette, his lips curving faintly—he had already foreseen the path this man would take in an hour. Waste? You want to step on me to build your reputation today, but tomorrow I'll teach you什么叫万劫不复.
